$comment: D-LIR-ASM-MEMORY-RESIDENT-FLOAT-OPERAND-CARRIED-AS-ITS-ADDRESS: a `long double` bound to the SIMD&FP asm constraint `"w"` must reach the template as its VALUE and leave it as one. On aarch64 Linux a `long double` is IEEE binary128, which DSS keeps in a 16-byte memory home; before the fix the asm expansion handed the template the home's ADDRESS — `low_half` compiled rc=0 and returned the bits of a stack address at debug AND release — and every shape that WRITES a long double register (`roundtrip`, `copy_q`, `swap`, `sel`) was refused at encode (A_NoMatchingEncodingVariant: the output register used as a base address). gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 compile the file and it runs exit 42 at -O0 and -O2 under qemu-aarch64. Five shapes: a `"+w"` round trip through an empty template, an input the template READS (`fmov %d0, %d1`), an output it WRITES (`mov %0.16b, %1.16b`), two outputs plus a `"+w"` tie plus a double operand in one statement (the second output read back as a result PIECE), and an `asm goto` whose output BOTH edges read. Every check is BITWISE over the value's own bytes and the values are built from bit patterns whose low 64 bits are not zero, so an address or a half-register carriage cannot pass; each failing check has its own exit code (11..17). RED-ON-DISABLE: make the binding treat a long double as register-resident again (the pre-fix carriage) -> both arm64 arms are refused again and `low_half` returns an address. ARM64 ONLY, on purpose: `"w"` is not a constraint letter x86_64 declares. The x86_64 half — an 80-bit x87 value on `"r"`, which gcc 13.3.0 carries in a general-register PAIR (64 + 16 bits) and DSS now carries the same way (D-ASM-MULTI-REGISTER-OPERAND-BINDING-NOT-REALIZED), and on `"x"`, which no reference carries and DSS refuses by name — is pinned in `lir/test_lir_asm_home_carriage` and run in `asm_value_operand_carriage_x86_64`. On Apple arm64 a `long double` IS a `double`, so the Mach-O arm is the ordinary-register control; it executes on the macOS leg.
